definition: An application built as one single unit instead of many small services.
exampleSentence: Our old monolith is hard to update because every change requires deploying the whole application.

definition: A design where parts of a system react to events instead of calling each other directly.
exampleSentence: With event-driven architecture, the billing service reacts as soon as an order is placed.

definition: A waiting line where programs leave messages for other programs to process later.
exampleSentence: Orders go into a message queue so the warehouse system can handle them one by one.

definition: A model where senders publish messages to a topic and subscribers receive them.
exampleSentence: We use Pub/Sub so any team can listen to new customer events without changing the sender.

definition: A single entry point that receives all API requests and sends them to the right service.
exampleSentence: The API gateway checks the token and then forwards each request to the correct service.

definition: A layer that manages, secures and monitors the communication between microservices.
exampleSentence: The service mesh encrypts all traffic between our services without changing their code.

definition: Storing every change as an event instead of saving only the latest state.
exampleSentence: With event sourcing, we can replay every change and see exactly how the account balance changed.

definition: A way of designing software around the real business concepts and language.
exampleSentence: Domain-driven design helped developers and sales people use the same words for the same things.

definition: A clear boundary inside which a word or model has one exact meaning.
exampleSentence: The word customer means something different in billing, so it lives in its own bounded context.

definition: Dividing a program into parts so that each part handles one clear job.
exampleSentence: Separation of concerns means the screen code should not contain database queries.

definition: A design where components depend on each other as little as possible.
exampleSentence: Loose coupling lets us replace the payment provider without touching the order code.

definition: When the parts of a module are closely related and focused on one purpose.
exampleSentence: A class with high cohesion is easy to name because it does only one thing.

definition: A proven, reusable solution to a common problem in software design.
exampleSentence: The observer is a design pattern that lets objects get notified when something changes.

definition: Passing the objects a class needs from outside instead of creating them inside.
exampleSentence: Dependency injection made the class easy to test because we could pass in a fake database.

definition: A property where repeating the same request has the same effect as sending it once.
exampleSentence: Idempotency ensures that a customer is not charged twice if the payment request is retried.

definition: A pattern that stops calling a failing service for a while so it can recover.
exampleSentence: The circuit breaker opened after ten errors, so the app stopped calling the broken payment service.

definition: A way for a slow part of a system to tell the sender to slow down.
exampleSentence: Backpressure protects the consumer by telling the producer to slow down when the queue is full.

definition: A rule saying a distributed system cannot guarantee consistency, availability and partition tolerance all at once.
exampleSentence: The CAP theorem explains why we must choose between strict consistency and always being available.

definition: A model where all copies of the data become equal after a short delay.
exampleSentence: Because of eventual consistency, a new profile photo may take a few seconds to appear everywhere.

definition: One operation that must succeed or fail across several different systems.
exampleSentence: A distributed transaction was needed to update both the payment system and the inventory.

definition: A way to manage a long operation across services using steps and undo actions.
exampleSentence: In the saga pattern, a failed shipment step triggers an action that refunds the payment.

definition: A protocol where all systems first agree to commit and then complete the change together.
exampleSentence: The two-phase commit made the operation safe but slow, because every system had to wait for the others.

definition: A method that lets users edit freely and checks for conflicts only when saving.
exampleSentence: Optimistic locking rejected my save because someone else had edited the record in the meantime.

definition: A method that locks a record as soon as someone starts to edit it.
exampleSentence: With pessimistic locking, nobody else can edit the invoice until the first person finishes.

definition: A lock that lets only one thread use a shared resource at a time.
exampleSentence: The thread must acquire the mutex before it writes to the shared file.

definition: A database setting that controls how much concurrent transactions can see of each other.
exampleSentence: We raised the isolation level to stop the report from reading half-finished updates.

definition: A log where a database first records changes so it can recover after a crash.
exampleSentence: After the power cut, the database used its write-ahead log to restore the last changes.

definition: A copy of a database used only for reading, to reduce the load on the main one.
exampleSentence: Reports now run on a read replica, so the main database stays fast for customers.

definition: Splitting a large table into smaller parts to make it faster and easier to manage.
exampleSentence: Partitioning the logs table by month made old data easy to delete.

definition: Adding duplicate data to a database on purpose to make reading faster.
exampleSentence: We used denormalization to store the customer name in the orders table and avoid a slow join.

definition: The part of a database that decides the fastest way to run a query.
exampleSentence: The query optimizer ignored our index because the table was too small to need it.

definition: An index that contains all the columns a query needs, so the table is not read.
exampleSentence: A covering index made the query ten times faster because the database never touched the table.

definition: Removing or updating stored cache data when the original data has changed.
exampleSentence: Cache invalidation is hard, because users still saw the old price after we changed it.

definition: A series of automated steps that move and transform data from one place to another.
exampleSentence: The nightly data pipeline collects sales files, cleans them and loads them into the warehouse.

definition: A controlled change to the structure of a database, such as adding a column.
exampleSentence: The schema migration adds a new column to the users table without any downtime.

definition: Splitting a large database across several servers, each holding part of the data.
exampleSentence: After sharding, each server stores only the customers from one region.

definition: Limiting how many requests a user or app can send in a given time.
exampleSentence: Rate limiting blocked the script after it sent a thousand requests in one minute.

definition: A program that receives messages from senders and delivers them to the right receivers.
exampleSentence: The message broker keeps messages safe until the receiving service is ready to process them.

definition: A special queue that stores messages that could not be processed successfully.
exampleSentence: Failed payment messages end up in the dead letter queue, where the team checks them every morning.

definition: The process by which servers in a group choose one to coordinate the others.
exampleSentence: After the main node crashed, leader election picked a new coordinator within seconds.
